subject: Post-call: buying route options and SOC 2 prerequisites
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lind <sara@vividhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: buying route options and SOC 2 prerequisites

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the buying path and the security gating items that will unblock procurement.

Recap:
- Vivid loved the latency/cost profile we showed for the 8k-context model in the demo.
- Main goal: pilot inference on customer-facing features (chat + reranking) with predictable unit economics.

Open qualification items I noted (please correct me if I missed anything):
1) Buying route preference: PO (standard) vs. corporate card vs. cloud marketplace. You mentioned procurement prefers PO but marketplace could speed up initial access — need confirmation.
2) Security gating: SOC 2 Type II report + executed DPA are required for production; you also indicated an internal security questionnaire we'll need to complete.
3) Timeline: you suggested a 3–5 week procurement cycle once legal/security items are satisfied.

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm whether the initial pilot can be provisioned via marketplace (faster) or if PO is required from day one.
- Me: share pricing summary, a draft mutual action plan (MAP), and SOC 2 report link.
- We: loop procurement/legal if PO is chosen.

I've attached a brief pricing summary and a lightweight MAP draft to accelerate internal review. If it helps, we can also prepare a marketplace pricing quote that aligns with your PO terms.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-summary.xlsx

If you can introduce the procurement contact (or reply-all with procurement@vividhealth.com), we’ll prepare the SOW/SLA language and aim to have a DocuSign-ready package within 48–72 business hours after legal review.

Thanks —
Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0129

---
Redwood Inference | High-throughput LLM inference.
From: Sara Lind <sara@vividhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@vividhealth.com, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@vividhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: buying route options and SOC 2 prerequisites

Hi Jonas —

Great to get this in writing. Quick answers from our side:
- Purchasing: our default is PO for any vendor engagement > $10k/year. For a pilot under $10k, we sometimes use the corporate card. We are open to marketplace for immediate access, but legal prefers PO + DPA before production.
- Security: SOC 2 Type II is required. I attached our standard security questionnaire — legal/security will run it alongside your SOC 2 report.
- Timeline: procurement estimate is ~4 weeks after we receive the completed questionnaire and the DPA draft.

Link to internal procurement: procurement@vividhealth.com (cc’d). Tom is our procurement lead — he’ll help with PO routing and required billing details.

I’ve attached the questionnaire. Please confirm whether Redwood has a standard DPA we can review, and point us to your SOC 2 report. Also, can you mark which buying route would let us start the pilot fastest (marketplace vs. card vs. PO)?

Thanks,
Sara Lind
Product Lead, VividHealth
sara@vividhealth.com

Attachments: Vivid_Security_Questionnaire.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lind <sara@vividhealth.com>, procurement@vividhealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: buying route options and SOC 2 prerequisites

Hi Sara / Tom —

Appreciate the clarity. Quick responses and a proposed plan so procurement/legal have everything in one thread.

Answers:
- Fastest pilot route: marketplace (if you can accept standard terms there) — we can provision within 24–48 hours.
- Card: fastest if spend is small, but we generally discourage for multi-month pilots due to invoice & visibility reasons.
- PO: standard for production and full-term pilots. If you choose PO, we’ll need PO number and billing contact to generate an invoice.

Security & docs:
- SOC 2 Type II: link to report — https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bREDWOODmap (redwood SOC 2 assets).
- DPA: Redwood’s standard DPA is available; I’ve attached a draft MAP that includes the legal milestones and proposed signoffs.
- Questionnaire: thanks for the attachment — Marissa (cc’d) from our legal/security team will assign an engineer to fill the technical sections and return a completed questionnaire within 3 business days.

Proposed mutual action plan (high level):
1) Marketplace pilot option: provision environment + test credentials (1–2 days) -> basic usage monitoring -> sign DPA if production proceeds.
2) PO route: we provide SOW + invoice -> Vivid issues PO -> Redwood signs DPA -> provisioning begins (timeline ~1–2 weeks once legal clears).

Next asks from Vivid:
- Confirm target buying route (marketplace / PO / card) for the pilot.
- If PO, please share PO contact and billing information (legal entity name, address, tax id if needed).

I attached: MAP-draft.docx and our pricing summary again for reference. Also linking DocuSign envelope where we usually finalize SOWs: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/12345ABC

Marissa / Karthik: flagging for questionnaire fill + commercial terms if Vivid prefers PO. I’ll coordinate the SOW and PO flow with Tom.

Thanks —
Jonas
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lind <sara@vividhealth.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@vividhealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: buying route options and SOC 2 prerequisites

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks for looping procurement in. From a legal/security perspective we can support either marketplace or PO for the pilot. A few practical notes:

- Marketplace: fastest to get you running; note that marketplace contracts are typically our standard terms and may limit custom SSO/integration SLAs until we agree a PO/SOW. If you want pilot telemetry tied to contract metrics, PO is cleaner.
- PO: acceptable. Please provide the legal entity name and PO contact. Our billing team will prepare an invoice once we have the PO number.
- DPA: attaching a redlines-ready DPA and a short SOW stub to accelerate review.
- Questionnaire: we’ll fill in the vendor answers and return the completed PDF. Expect the completed questionnaire back by end of day Wednesday.

Attachments: SOW-stub.pdf

Action items for Vivid:
1) Tell us which route you want to use for the pilot (marketplace / PO / card).
2) If PO, share billing details and PO contact.

If it helps, we can run a brief 30-minute procurement touchpoint with Tom to walk through the MAP and timelines. Jonas, can you coordinate availability?

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
-- End of thread --
